newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end lower wiping out gains,Btps weigh.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end lower wiping out gains,Btps weigh.

text.p: Italian stocks ended easier but off session lows on Tuesday, wiping out gains made earlier in the session, unable to find buyers to sustain an opening bounce higher with weaker Italian bond futures weighing on sentiment, traders said.

"The market lost ground after being unable to sustain the early firmer trend. Wall Street's rise was ignored, there was a lack of buying orders and Btp futures also pared their earlier gains on the back of weaker T-bonds," one dealer said.

The All-share Mibtel index ended off 0.28 percent at 10,345 after a high of 10,449 and 10,332 low. The Mib30 blue chip index ended down 0.41 percent at 15,416 after a peak at 15,600 and low at 15,385.

Carlo De Benedetti's financial holding Cofide and industrial holding Cir gained strongly against the trend. Cofide was up 9.26 percent at 885 lire and Cir ended 8.37 percent higher at 1,002, in the wake of Luigi Giribaldi upping his Cofide stake.

News the Monaco-based businessman had raised his stake to 20.05 in Cofide emerged last week. "The strategy is not clear but everything points to a redefining of the group's profile," one analyst said. De Benedetti and a syndicate of shareholders holds 56.7 percent of Cofide shares.
Olivetti also firmed, ending up 0.8 percent at 519.6.

Fiat closed 1.85 percent lower near the day's low at 4,303 lire after a steady start despite Italian new car registration data for November showing an overall fall of 11 percent and a decline of Fiat marques of 17 percent.
Traders said the figures were not a great surprise but Fiat lost ground when the market turned into negative territory.
Telecom stocks saw late selling after having supported the market in the early part of the session, but mobile phone operator TIM rose 1.12 percent to 3,622 lire.
Energy group ENI lost 0.55 percent to 7,785 lire.
